# Steam locomotive (`steam_locomotive`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/navigation.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Navigation, transport & exploration (`navigation`)
- Deps: needs high_pressure_steam, railway; helped by crank_connecting_rod, coal_mining
- Core idea: A high-pressure boiler on wheels drives pistons that turn the wheels directly through cranks; exhaust steam blown up the chimney (blastpipe) draws the fire, and many fire tubes through the boiler raise steam fast (Stephenson's Rocket, 1829). Early engines ran on cast iron, whose brittle rails could break under the load. Heavier traffic favoured wrought iron and later steel. Fuel, water stops and braking limited practical service.
- Pitfalls:
  - A low-pressure Watt engine on wheels; it is far too heavy for its power
  - Boilers without safety valves and fusible plugs
  - Assuming smooth wheels will not grip rails; they do, with moderate gradients and enough weight on the driving wheels
- History: europe: 1804 – Trevithick's Penydarren locomotive; 1813 Puffing Billy; 1825 Stephenson's Locomotion; 1829 Rocket at the Rainhill trials
- Read:
  - Samuel Smiles, The Life of George Stephenson (1857)
  - L. T. C. Rolt, George and Robert Stephenson: The Railway Revolution (1960)
